clue.text: True populism in a way is serving many aims

indicators.note: in a way suggests the letters of the words true populism set out in some other way, a fresh order

explanation.surface: A political commentator remarks that genuine populism somehow manages to pursue lots of goals at once.
explanation.definitionFit: Something with several uses or functions is said to serve many aims at once.

clue.text: Male unusually solicitous about girl's head is an expert at scoring?

indicators.note: about says the rearranged letters wrap around the next piece
unusually says the letters of solicitous appear in an unusual order
the girl's head is the first letter of the word girl

explanation.surface: A man who is oddly attentive around a young woman is supposedly an expert at 'scoring' with her.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusually' signals the anagram and 'about' puts the head of 'girl's' inside it. 'Scoring' is music-writing here, not romantic success; the question mark flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: A scholar of music studies scores, the written parts for instruments, so is a sort of expert at scoring.

clue.text: Solitary individual — one making advances, it's reported

indicators.note: it's reported says the clue's lender word sounds like the entry when spoken

parts.note: a lender, one who advances money, is a loaner

explanation.surface: A solitary figure is rumoured to be the one making romantic or financial advances.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who prefers their own company and keeps away from others is a solitary individual.

clue.text: Something intentionally burnt to be very annoying

definitions.meaning: aromatic resin or sticks burnt on purpose for their fragrant smoke
as a verb, to enrage or infuriate someone

explanation.surface: A deliberately burnt thing is enough to be extremely irritating.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun is perfumed material burnt in worship; the verb, stressed on the second syllable, means to make furious.

clue.text: Straighten out upper-class knight about web address

parts.note: U is the standard label for upper-class usage
N is the chess notation for a knight
C is short for circa, Latin for about
a URL is the address of a web page

explanation.surface: A posh knight sorts out a muddle concerning a website address.
explanation.definitionFit: To unroll or flatten something coiled is to straighten it out.

clue.text: Send up some weak lopsided dance

indicators.note: Send up says the hidden letters are read backwards
some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone is told to mock a feeble, lurching bit of dancing.
explanation.definitionFit: A lively Bohemian dance in duple time, popular in nineteenth-century ballrooms, is a classic example of a dance.

clue.text: One attending tea party after small break

indicators.note: after says the guest comes behind the abbreviation for small

parts.note: the Mad Hatter attends the mad tea party in Alice in Wonderland

explanation.surface: A guest at a tea party gets there after a short break.
explanation.definitionFit: To smash something into pieces is to break it.

clue.text: New EU money to encourage highly-skilled operator

parts.note: euros are the currency of the European Union
to urge on is to encourage

explanation.surface: Fresh European Union funding is meant to spur on some highly skilled worker.
explanation.definitionFit: A brain surgeon is a specialist who performs operations, so an operator in the surgical sense.

clue.text: Boy in charge of sound

parts.note: a son is a boy

explanation.surface: A boy has been put in charge of the audio.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes things relating to sound waves or audible noise.

clue.text: Picture educational establishment with area for English

indicators.note: with introduces the new letter that comes into the word
for says the new letter stands in place of the abbreviation for English

parts.note: a college is a place of further or higher education

explanation.surface: Someone describes a picture of a school where a space has been set aside for English lessons.
explanation.definitionFit: An artwork made by sticking assorted scraps onto a surface is a kind of picture.

clue.text: Awkward situation about old official at inquest

indicators.note: about says the awkward-situation word goes around the letter for old

parts.note: to be in a corner is to be in an awkward situation

explanation.surface: A tricky situation arises concerning an elderly official at an inquest.
explanation.definitionFit: The officer who investigates sudden or suspicious deaths presides over the inquest.

clue.text: In pursuit of more at the back?

definitions.meaning: the comparative of aft, the nautical word for towards the stern, so further back

explanation.surface: Chasing something, perhaps more at the rear.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is a whimsical one: aft means at the back of a ship, so its comparative would mean more at the back; the question mark admits the stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: As a preposition it means following in pursuit; as a sailing adjective it means further toward the stern.

clue.text: Genuine backing on both sides of the road for food store

indicators.note: on both sides of says the reversed letters are split around the road abbreviation
backing says the word for genuine is read from the end

parts.note: something genuine is real
RD is the standard abbreviation for road

explanation.surface: Real support from both sides of the street for a local food shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' gives LAER, which 'on both sides of' splits in two to flank the road abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A pantry or cool room for keeping provisions is a food store in the home.

clue.text: Rake grabbing money exactly as usual

indicators.note: grabbing says the rake word closes around the money word

parts.note: a rake is a dissolute man, a roué
tin is old slang for money

explanation.surface: A womaniser snatches some cash, just as he always does.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done to the regular pattern, with nothing unusual, is exactly as usual.

clue.text: Singers in church or university society

explanation.surface: Singers perform either in church or for a university society.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of people singing together, as in a choir, is a body of singers.

clue.text: Livery? It's back in cheap supply

indicators.note: in says the reversed pair sits inside the rearranged letters
supply is read as the adverb of supple, so the letters of cheap bend into a new order
back says the letters of it are read in reverse

parts.note: the word It gives the letters; the 's is just is, linking the pieces

explanation.surface: A livery company's supplies are being bought back cheaply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supply' is an anagram signal (in a supple way), giving HEPAC; 'back' and 'in' place the reversed pair before its last letter. 'Livery' is read as liver-y, to do with the liver.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means relating to the liver, which the clue jokily spells as livery.

clue.text: What killer might do to act as leader

parts.note: to be something is to act as it
a head is a leader

explanation.surface: A murderer's motive might be to take charge as the boss.
explanation.definitionFit: Cutting off someone's head is one method an executioner or murderer might use.

clue.text: Good rule for processing poor food

indicators.note: processing means working the letters of rule through into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A sound rule for food manufacturing is applied to some unappetising grub.
explanation.definitionFit: A thin watery porridge, as served in workhouses, is a byword for meagre food.

clue.text: Beer left to mature — right

parts.note: to age is to mature

explanation.surface: A brewer leaves the beer to mature, and rightly so.
explanation.definitionFit: A light, bottom-fermented beer, stored to mature, is a common type of beer.

clue.text: Ruler pre-Rome? That must be wrong

indicators.note: must be wrong says the letters of pre-Rome are not in the right order and need rearranging

explanation.surface: A historian doubts the claim that a certain ruler predated Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: The supreme ruler of an empire, such as a Roman Caesar, is a monarch.

clue.text: Law scholar losing time in talk

indicators.note: losing says the time letter is dropped from the talk word

parts.note: to rabbit is British slang for to chatter on

explanation.surface: A legal academic is wasting time chatting.
explanation.walkthrough: To rabbit (on) is everyday British slang for talking at length.
explanation.definitionFit: A Jewish religious teacher is learned in Jewish law, so a scholar of law.

clue.text: Hearts set in individual stones

indicators.note: set in says the hearts letter is placed inside the individual word

parts.note: single means individual
H is the abbreviation for hearts, the card suit

explanation.surface: Heart-shaped gems are mounted in separate stones.
explanation.definitionFit: Small rounded pebbles, as on a beach, are a mass of stones.

clue.text: Firm exporting small item of furniture

indicators.note: exporting says the small letter is sent out of the firm word

parts.note: firm means steady, stable

explanation.surface: A company shipping a little piece of furniture overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Firm' looks like a company, but it is the adjective STABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat-topped piece of furniture on legs, for eating or working at, is a familiar item.

clue.text: Drop round professional copy

indicators.note: round says the drop word goes around the professional word

parts.note: a reduction is a drop
pro is short for professional

explanation.surface: Drop by and do a quick round of copying for a professional.
explanation.definitionFit: A replica of an original painting or piece of furniture is a copy.
